variants.headline: Builder signs for a new project
variants.sub: A construction contract for {project} has been awarded to {builder}.
variants.body:
The builder {builder} has signed a contract for {project} at an agreed price of {price}. The signature establishes an undertaking to build, not a completed building. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the award from delivery, while taking seriously the obligations the agreement is meant to create.

A builder, a project and an agreed price. Those are solid terms for a story, but they are not a finished building. Readers can welcome a signed undertaking without letting the ceremony move the project all the way to completion. The difficult part is still what a contract is for.

The handling of {target} should be assessed against the signed undertaking. This paper records the award and agreed price without announcing a construction result that the contract itself has not yet delivered. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
